newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada makes cash offer for Clyde.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada makes cash offer for Clyde.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said on Wednesday it was making a cash offer of 105 pence per share for Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc, valuing the company at 432 million pounds. It said the offer represented a premium of 24.3 percent over the mid-market quotation for a Clyde share of 84 1/2 pence at close of trading on December 17.
The group said in a statement that by December 17, it owned 7.4 million Clyde shares, representing around 1.8 percent of the oil and gas exploration company's issued share capital.

"The offer for Clyde follows Gulf Canada's previously stated desire to increase its activities outside of its existing core areas of North America and Indonesia," J. P. Bryan, president and chief executive of Gulf Canada said.

Gulf Canada, a Canadian-based oil and natural gas exploration and production company, said Clyde's North Sea and Australian assets would provide it with additional core areas, and Clyde's Indonesian assets would complement its existing assets.
By 0820 GMT, shares in Clyde had shot ahead 27 pence to stand at 111-1/2 pence.
